source.snippet: I'm writing this after receiving a Vercel bill that was 10x higher than usual. The worst part: The increase wasn't caused by more users, but by +1M requests from meta-externalagent/1.1. The requests targeted a Vercel preview deployment that we had shared on WhatsApp to test whether its link-preview metadata was working correctly. We naively never bothered with bot calls; they had never caused any problems in the previous four years of our app on Vercel, but that changed when Meta's crawler...

problem_statement: Businesses hosting apps on Vercel (and similar edge/serverless platforms) receive unexpectedly massive bills caused by aggressive crawl bots—such as Meta's link-preview agent—hammering preview deployments, with no built-in cost-cap or bot-filtering layer to prevent runaway spend.
target_segment: Small-to-mid-size SaaS and product teams using Vercel, Netlify, or similar serverless/edge hosting who pay per-request and lack dedicated bot-management infrastructure.
notes: Direct paying-customer pain: operator reports a 10x bill spike from a single bot user-agent on a platform they pay per request. Comments indicate others have experienced similar. Competing approaches (Cloudflare WAF, custom middleware) exist but require setup expertise. Opportunity: a lightweight, zero-config bot-shield layer or middleware package specifically for Vercel/edge deployments with a cost-cap alert tier. Buyer is a paying Vercel customer already spending money on hosting.
